_note: Example walkthrough for the shipped RISC-V example corpus. Copy it, then replace the queries and expected sources with ones from your own corpus. expectSource is a substring of the cited document name, so split parts still match.
title: Developer docs in the editor — grounded, cited, figures included

steps.title: Prose lookup
steps.say: A developer asks a reference-manual question without leaving the editor. The answer cites the exact document and section.
steps.query: What does the dmcontrol register control in the Debug Module?

steps.title: Cross-document routing
steps.say: Two manuals are indexed together. The question routes to the right one, with no bleed from the other.
steps.query: What is the encoding format of the RISC-V compressed instruction set?

steps.title: Answer that only exists in a figure
steps.say: This answer lives in a register diagram, not in the prose. A text-only pipeline throws the diagram away; here it comes back as a searchable description.
steps.query: What is the bit width of the mtime register and which bits does it span?

steps.title: Deep section
steps.say: Citations stay precise even several heading levels down.
steps.query: How does the JTAG Debug Transport Module encode DMI operations?

steps.title: Out of corpus
steps.say: When the documents don't cover something, the honest answer is 'not found', not a confident guess.
steps.query: What is the recommended torque for the enclosure mounting screws?
